title: Gabriele Orrico — 'A mission can survive its founder and still fail the people it exists to serve'
summary: Executive Gabriele Orrico, part of the Incorruptible community, extends the book's thesis with a distinctive follow-on question: once a mission is protected, who gets to interpret it? Founder intent, successor reading, and employee experience can diverge; whoever controls what the mission means holds considerable power over whom it serves. 21 likes, 8-comment discussion thread.
blockquote: A mission can survive its founder and still fail the people it exists to serve. … Who gets to challenge the interpretation without being accused of disloyalty? Because whoever controls what the mission means has considerable power over whom it serves.
